global_parameter.name: usb audio
global_parameter.tooltip: what the minichord does with the sound of the phone or computer it is plugged into. 0: as it always has, it is offered as a speaker and what is sent to it is not played (a phone sends all its sound there, and goes quiet). 1: it is played through the minichord, beside the instrument, for playing along. 2: it is not offered as a speaker, so the phone or computer keeps its own sound. In every case the minichord's own sound can be recorded over USB. A setting of the instrument, not of a preset: it stays as chosen whichever preset is loaded. Changing to or from 2 restarts the minichord a moment later, since the phone or computer only learns what it offers when it connects

global_parameter.name: retrigger chords
global_parameter.tooltip: defines whether the chords will be retriggered when playing a modulation of the current chord or in continuous chord mode

global_parameter.name: change held strings
global_parameter.tooltip: defines whether a held harp note will change when changing chord

global_parameter.name: slash level

global_parameter.name: transpose

global_parameter.name: barry harris mode
global_parameter.tooltip: change major chords to major 6, the minor chords to minor 6, and the diminished chords to fully diminished. Recommanded to use the fourth harp shuffling array

global_parameter.name: chord frame shift
global_parameter.tooltip: shifts the register frame up (e.g. 1 makes D the lowest pitched, 2 makes E the lowest pitched, and so on)

global_parameter.name: chord key signature
global_parameter.tooltip: automatically makes flat or sharp the chords for a particular key. 0=C, 1=G, 2=D, 3=A, 4=E, 5=B, 6=F, 7=Bb, 8=Eb, 9=Ab, 10=Db, 11=Gb

global_parameter.name: scalar harp mode
global_parameter.tooltip: what the harp strings play. 0=follows the chord (default), 1=Major, 2=Major Pentatonic, 3=Minor Pentatonic, 4=Diminished 6th, 5=Relative Natural Minor, 6=Relative Harmonic Minor, 7=Relative Minor Pentatonic, 8=scale chosen per chord, 9=as 8 but pentatonic

global_parameter.name: chord inversion
global_parameter.tooltip: voicing of the chord buttons. 0 is root position, 1 and 2 are the first and second inversions, 3 is the third inversion for seventh and sixth chords or the root position an octave up for triads
global_parameter.method: chord_inversion=value; for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) { current_chord_notes[i]=calculate_note_chord(i,slash_chord,sharp_active); } for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) { if (chord_envelope_array[i]->isActive()) { set_chord_voice_frequency(i, current_chord_notes[i]); } }

global_parameter.name: chord spacing
global_parameter.tooltip: how far apart the chord voices sit. 0=close (adjacent tones), 1=drop 2, 2=drop 3, 3=drop 2 and 4 (the most evenly spread), 4=spread the outer voices. Drops move a voice down an octave; a move that would leave the usable range is not made
global_parameter.method: chord_spacing=value; for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) { current_chord_notes[i]=calculate_note_chord(i,slash_chord,sharp_active); } for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) { if (chord_envelope_array[i]->isActive()) { set_chord_voice_frequency(i, current_chord_notes[i]); } }

global_parameter.name: vocoder
global_parameter.tooltip: the chords (or the harp, see vocoder carrier) take on the shape of the sound coming in over USB, so they talk or sing with it: speech, singing or drums from the phone or computer. In percent of the vocoded sound in place of the dry; 0 is off, as before. The minichord has no microphone, so the voice has to come over USB, which needs usb audio 0 or 1 (0: only the vocoded chords are heard; 1: the incoming sound is heard too). With nothing coming in, the vocoded part is silent

global_parameter.name: vocoder carrier
global_parameter.tooltip: what the vocoder shapes. 0: the chords, the classic sustained vocoder sound. 1: the harp, whose plucks die away too fast to carry words well but make textures. 2: both, the harp's vocoded part coming through the chords' effects

global_parameter.name: vocoder consonants
global_parameter.tooltip: how much of the incoming sound's hiss (s, t, sh) the vocoder lets through, so words can be made out. 0 is a pure vocoder, only the chords' own sound
